title: pr-902345-onboard-voyagerx-25b-v1.0-perf-metadata-changelog-automation
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Onboard VoyagerX-25B v1.0: metadata, performance profiles, and changelog automation. Adds baseline perf profile (latency/throughput), quantization recommendations, and automated changelog entry generation.
body:
Summary: Onboard VoyagerX-25B v1.0 into the model registry with full metadata, performance profiles produced by the perf lab, and automated changelog/release-notes wiring. Motivation: VoyagerX-25B is a widely requested model variant with improved quality/efficiency for long-context workloads; we want reproducible perf profiles and automatic changelog entries to reduce manual release work.

What this PR does:
- Adds canonical metadata YAML for voyagerx-25b v1.0 (parameters, tokenizer, provenance, default serving config).
- Adds perf profile JSON that captures latency and throughput at representative batch and sequence lengths, plus recommended quantization profiles and kernel hints.
- Hooks the new model into the changelog automation pipeline so onboarding emits a draft release note entry under changelogs/drafts/.
- Adds a perf unit test and a CI perf-check job to validate profile schema and sample latency thresholds.
- Updates docs/models/voyagerx.md with public-facing description and example code snippet.

Checklist:
- [x] Metadata schema validated against registry schema.yaml
- [x] Perf profile generated from benchmark-lab runs and reviewed by perf eng
- [x] Changelog automation produces draft entry and labels it for product review
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Unit tests added

Related: ENG-4123 (onboarding playbook), ENG-4189 (perf profile schema updates), SUP-7210 (customer request).

CI: initial run flagged a flaky perf-schema-test (timeout) - increased test timeout and re-ran pipeline. All checks passing on latest run.

Notes for reviewer: focus review on correctness of metadata fields (model ID/name, tokenizer details, provenance link), sanity of perf numbers (we included raw benchmark metadata in the perf JSON), and that the changelog automation template contains the required release-note placeholders (impact, migration notes, recommended runtimes).

If approved, merge with squash to keep registry history atomic.
